name: Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd.
monetization: Sells the domestic full stack — Ascend accelerators (with in-house HBM), Atlas SuperPoDs, Kunpeng CPUs, MindSpore/CANN software, and Huawei Cloud — as China's sanctioned-market Nvidia substitute.
description_md: Huawei is the employee-owned Chinese technology group (2024 revenue RMB 862B) that anchors China's parallel AI compute stack. Its HiSilicon-designed Ascend accelerators (910C shipping; 950 series with **in-house-developed HBM** from 2026) are fabricated at SMIC on non-EUV 7nm-class processes, assembled into Atlas SuperPoD rack systems marketed against Nvidia's NVL platforms. Huawei has been on the US Entity List since May 2019 — the original export-control action — and its resurgence in AI chips is the central counterexample to the controls' effectiveness. DeepSeek's V4 launched with day-0 training and serving on Ascend in April 2026.
ai_monetization_md: Hardware sales of Ascend accelerators and Atlas systems to Chinese clouds, labs, telcos, and state buyers — a market progressively reserved for domestic silicon as US bans tightened (H20 re-ban dynamics, B30A blocked, offshore-DC ban Jun 2026; TrendForce expects domestic chips at ~50% of China's high-end AI market by end-2026). Planned 2026 output: ~600K Ascend 910C units (~2× 2025) and up to 1.6M total Ascend dies across SKUs. Beyond chips: Huawei Cloud sells Ascend-backed AI services; the CANN/MindSpore stack monetizes lock-in the way CUDA does. Financial detail is limited — Huawei is private and does not break out Ascend revenue (a known data gap).
ai_strategy_md: Vertical integration under embargo: own the accelerator (Ascend), the memory (in-house HBM on the 950 series — bypassing the Korean/US HBM chokepoint), the interconnect and rack (SuperPoD), the software (CANN), and the fab relationship (SMIC's constrained 7nm capacity is largely allocated to Huawei). Compensate for per-chip performance deficits with system-level scale (larger pods, more power) and price. Win the domestic market by policy default, then export to sanctioned-adjacent markets. DeepSeek V4's day-0 Ascend support is the flagship proof that frontier-class work can run on the stack.
risk_notes_md: **Manufacturing ceiling:** without EUV, SMIC's 7nm-class output caps both volume and efficiency; the ~600K 910C plan depends on SMIC yield/capacity doubling and remains press-reported, not disclosed. **HBM gap:** in-house HBM is unproven at scale versus SK hynix/Samsung parts; CXMT's HBM ramp timing is unverified. **Entity List:** US restrictions (since May 2019, repeatedly expanded) bar access to leading-edge foundry, tools, and most foreign components; June 2026 offshore rules also complicate customers' hybrid strategies, which helps Huawei domestically but caps its addressable market. **Opacity:** private company; no audited segment data — most figures here carry press-reported confidence.

observations.notes: ~2× the ~300K produced in 2025; total Ascend dies across SKUs reported up to 1.6M for 2026. Fabricated at SMIC.
Group revenue (all segments), +22% y/y; Huawei does not disclose Ascend/AI revenue separately. CY2025 figures not yet in this record.

events.title: Added to the US Entity List
events.why_it_matters: The founding event of the export-control era: cut Huawei off from US technology and leading-edge foundry, forcing the vertical-integration strategy that now defines China's AI stack.

events.title: Unveils Ascend 950 with in-house HBM for 2026; SuperPoD roadmap against Nvidia
events.why_it_matters: Attacks the HBM bottleneck — the one input China could not source — with vertical integration; the SuperPoD roadmap concedes per-chip deficits and competes at system level.

events.title: DeepSeek V4 trains and serves on Ascend from day 0
events.why_it_matters: The strongest demand-side validation of the Ascend stack: China's flagship open-weight frontier model no longer depends on Nvidia hardware at any stage.

sources.notes: Export-control frame: offshore-DC ban extension, Jun 2026.
